name: Paschal Lamb Typical Nature Of
overview: The Paschal Lamb, as outlined in Exodus 12, is a male lamb of the first year, chosen without blemish and kept until the fourteenth day of the month before being killed in the evening by the assembly. Its blood was to be applied specifically to the doorposts and lintel of the houses where it was eaten, symbolizing protection and obedience. The lamb was to be roasted with fire and eaten with unleavened bread and bitter herbs, not raw or boiled, and consumed in haste with readiness for departure, reflecting a type of Christ who was without blemish, sacrificed at the appointed time, and whose blood brings deliverance.
